Your moodboard recipe

Keep it connected

Use this mix to give the rest of your campaign a clear visual direction.

1
3–5 coloursAdd HEX codes so you can reuse the exact shades later.
2
2 complementary fontsChoose one for headings and one that keeps body text easy to read.
3
4–6 purposeful imagesEvery image should fit the cause, audience and intended mood.
4
Repeatable visual detailsInclude shapes, textures or icons you could reuse in later products.
Aim for connected, not crowded. A moodboard should help another designer make consistent choices.

Build the Brand key terms

Brand identityThe visual and verbal features that help people recognise an organisation and understand what it represents.
House styleA consistent set of rules for logo, colour, typography, imagery, layout and tone.
LogoA recognisable symbol, wordmark or combination used to identify an organisation.
MoodboardA planned collection of imagery, colours, type and textures that communicates a visual direction.
Colour paletteA limited group of colours selected to work together consistently.
TypographyThe selection and arrangement of typefaces to communicate tone and make text readable.
ImageryThe photographs, illustrations, icons and visual style used by a brand.
AdaptableAble to work successfully at different sizes, on different backgrounds and across different products.
ContrastA clear visual difference that helps elements stand out and remain readable.
CoherentConsistent and logically connected, with every visual choice feeling part of the same identity.
